notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08. Routine EGRESS_BLOCKED/ENOTFOUND on most org-domain WebFetch attempts; platform.claude.com/docs was directly fetchable and confirmed no new near-term Claude retirement dates beyond what's already filed. Search-index coverage for same-day (Oct 7/8) news was thin across all four labs/vendors, so this run leans forward-looking: policy deadlines (EU AI Act Annex III delay, Colorado's rewritten AI law), 2027 conference dates (ICLR, Davos, MWC Barcelona, DEF CON, Black Hat), cert-lifetime policy milestones, and GitHub/AWS/Azure/Google Cloud engineering changes dated this week. Several strong candidates were dropped as exact or near-duplicates of what's already on the calendar (Amazon Bedrock AI21 Jamba 1.5, OpenAI gpt-image family, Google Play target API level extension, Claude Haiku 5.5 availability restated via AWS) rather than risk clutter.
concerns: Standing duplicate, not introduced this run: data/events/2027-01.json carries THREE separate active entries for essentially the same Google Play Contacts/Location/SMS policy change, all dated 2027-01-27 — 'google-play-contacts-and-location-permissions-policy-changes-2027-01', 'google-play-contacts-location-permission-policy-takes-effect-2027-01', and 'google-play-retires-phone-call-verification-via-read-call-lo-2027-01'. This run's devtools/cloud and mobile lanes both independently turned up a fourth near-identical source (developer.android.com/distribute/play-policies, listing the same Jan 27 2027 date plus a geofencing change not captured in any of the three existing entries) but it was deliberately NOT filed to avoid adding a fourth near-duplicate to an already-unresolved cluster. First flagged in the 2026-10-01 run's concerns (still unresolved as of today) — a maintainer should consolidate these three into one entry (the geofencing-API change is the one piece of genuinely new information to fold in) and this is the same src/lib/id.ts isSameThing token-overlap issue flagged in multiple prior runs' logs.

A Google Developer Forum thread reports the Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite retirement date is given as October 16, 2026 by one Google surface (Gemini Developer API, already filed as 'Google extends Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite retirement to October 16' at confirmed confidence) but as October 20, 2026 by another (Vertex AI model lifecycle page), with a report that the live page briefly showed 'no shutdown date announced' for Flash-Lite. Not re-filed given the conflict; a maintainer with working fetch access to ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations and the Vertex AI lifecycle page should reconcile which surface's date is authoritative before the existing entry is touched again.

An EU AI Act finding (Digital Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 delaying Annex III high-risk obligations from August 2026 to December 2, 2027, with the Annex I embedded-product deadline pushed to August 2, 2028) was researched and well-sourced (Cloud Security Alliance, Gibson Dunn, both citing the regulation itself) but falls outside today's 12-month filing window (which runs through 2027-10-08) and was dropped rather than chased further, per the run instructions. Worth picking up in a sweep closer to November/December 2027 — it is a separate fact from the already-filed 'EU AI Act full compliance deadline for pre-existing general-purpose AI models' (2027-08-02), which concerns GPAI obligations, not Annex III high-risk systems.

Five candidates found by this run's lanes (MWC Barcelona 2027, CA/Browser Forum's 100-day TLS certificate cap, DEF CON 35, Black Hat USA 2027, and Let's Encrypt's 64-day default certificate lifetime) turned out to already be on the calendar, filed with equal or better sourcing — a sign the lanes are rediscovering the same well-known 2027 conference/policy dates each run. The Let's Encrypt one is worth a maintainer's attention: a --dry-run with the title 'Let's Encrypt shortens default certificate lifetime to 64 days' / org 'Internet Security Research Group (Let's Encrypt)' did NOT merge against the existing 'Let's Encrypt switches default certificate profile to 64-day validity' / org 'Let's Encrypt' entry at the same 2027-02-10 date — sameTitle's 0.6 Jaccard floor only saw 3 of ~10 distinct tokens shared ('default', 'certificate', '64'), well under threshold, so it would have silently created a second, duplicate row rather than updating the existing one. Caught only because this run's author happened to run `npm run validate:data` and noticed two near-identical warnings; a maintainer should consider whether sameTitle needs a lower floor or a synonym/stemming pass (shortens/switches, lifetime/profile/validity) for this kind of paraphrase-level duplicate risk, distinct from the version-number token issue flagged in prior runs. Not re-filed this run.

GitHub's own changelog post titled 'X25519-only TLS ends for GHE.com on October 7' (filed below) has a URL slug reading '...-on-september-15' — an apparent authoring inconsistency on GitHub's own page. Filed with the October 7 date since that's what the title and body both state, but flagging in case a future search surfaces a conflicting September 15 version of the same change.

OpenAI's realtime/audio model family retirement (gpt-realtime, gpt-4o-realtime, gpt-audio, gpt-4o-audio), reportedly January 20, 2027, was investigated but NOT filed: one third-party tracker explicitly stated this date was no longer present when they re-checked OpenAI's live deprecations page, a direct contradiction serious enough to skip rather than file a confidence level that might be a lie. Worth a maintainer's direct check of developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.
